test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 19 Sept 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Which of the following defines the functions of the Reserve Bank of India?

A. It issues the currency of the country.

B. It regulates the country’s monetary policy through various instruments.

C. It acts as a banker to the government.

D. It collects deposits from the public and lends loans to those who want to take loans by keeping a certain percentage of their deposits.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1: A, B and C**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is the central bank of the country, and it performs several crucial functions to ensure the smooth functioning of the financial system.
 
• One of the primary functions of the RBI is to issue and regulate the currency of the country, ensuring adequate circulation of money in the economy.
 
• The RBI regulates the country's monetary policy using various instruments such as the repo rate, reverse repo rate, and others to control inflation and stabilize the economy.
 
• It also acts as a banker to the government, managing its accounts, and providing loans when necessary.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Currency Issuance:**

 
 
• The RBI has the sole authority to issue currency notes in India, except for one-rupee notes and coins, which are issued by the Ministry of Finance. This function ensures a stable and uniform currency system across the country.
 
 
 
• **Monetary Policy Regulation:**
 
 
• The RBI formulates and implements monetary policy to control the supply of money and interest rates. Key tools include the repo rate, reverse repo rate, cash reserve ratio (CRR), and statutory liquidity ratio (SLR).
 
• These tools help manage inflation, encourage investment, and promote economic growth.
 
 
 
• **Banker to the Government:**
 
 
• The RBI manages the banking needs of both the central and state governments. It handles the government's banking transactions, including the receipt and payment of funds and the management of public debt.
 
 
 
• **Public Deposits and Loans:**
 
 
• While the RBI does not collect deposits from the public or lend loans directly to individuals, it regulates and supervises the banking sector to ensure financial stability and consumer protection.
 
• Commercial banks and other financial institutions perform these functions under the regulatory framework established by the RBI.
